change.author: nicktrn

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves 2FA enabled but the page stale
findings.body: After a successful enable, the step becomes DisplayBackupCodes and `onEnable()` is only called from the Close button (line ~269). The Dialog still has `onOpenChange`, so Esc or an outside click closes it. In `apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:62-72`, `onOpenChange` only toggles `enableModalOpen`. That skips `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()`, so the switch keeps showing disabled although 2FA is now enabled on the server. The component also stays mounted, so reopening it shows the backup-codes step again. The user can lose the only copy of the codes. Handle dismissal on this step the same way as Close: call `onEnable()` and `resetState()`, or block dismissal until Close is clicked.

findings.title: Backup code is consumed with a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The codes are read, one is nulled, and the whole encrypted blob is written back. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass `indexOf` before either update lands, so a single-use code works twice. A conditional update, or a transaction with a row lock, would close this. The same pattern is in `disable.ts`, which deletes everything afterwards, so it matters less there.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in the request body causes a 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws a TypeError when the client sends a non-string truthy value such as a number or object. Check `typeof === "string"` and return IncorrectBackupCode instead. The same applies to `credentials.backupCode` in next-auth-options.ts:144, although credentials there are form strings.

findings.title: Message points to a settings action that does not exist
findings.body: `missing_backup_codes` says "Please generate them in your settings". This PR adds no UI to generate or regenerate codes. Backup codes are only created inside the enable flow (setup.ts), so users who enabled 2FA before this PR have `backupCodes` null and no way to get codes short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA. The message sends them to a feature that is not there. Either add regeneration or reword the message.

findings.title: Toggle button may submit the form
findings.body: The new "Lost access" / "Go back" Button is inside `<Form>` and has no `type="button"`. If the UI Button defaults to type submit, clicking it would submit the disable request. Please confirm the default or set the type explicitly. The login.tsx footer buttons sit outside the form, so they are not affected.

contracts.equivalent_path: Previously onEnable() was called directly after TOTP verification (two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68 closes the modal and invalidates viewer.me).
contracts.before_after: Before: enable success closed the modal and refreshed state. After: it only does so via the Close button; Esc or an outside click goes through onOpenChange, which only toggles open.
contracts.visible_effect: The switch stays stale and the modal reopens on the codes step.
contracts.failure_mode: Dismissal without Close loses the codes and leaves the UI out of sync.

contracts.equivalent_path: TOTP branch immediately below (line 157) and disable.ts TOTP branch.
contracts.before_after: Login verifies the password, rate-limits, then consumes the code. Disable verifies the password, then deletes all codes with 2FA.
contracts.visible_effect: Errors map to IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes messages.
contracts.failure_mode: Concurrent reuse is possible; a non-string body gives a 500.

summary: Backup-code login and disable follow the existing TOTP paths. One real bug: dismissing the enable dialog on the backup-codes step (Esc or outside click) skips onEnable, so the settings page stays stale and the user can lose the codes. Smaller points: non-atomic single-use consumption, a non-string `backupCode` body causes a 500, the missing-codes message points to a settings action that doesn't exist, and a possible form-submit on the new toggle button. I did not read the UI Button component, so the last point is unconfirmed.
